Curated datasets at data.rmorie.com

Source: R/data_hub.R
hostcat.Rd

Beyond the open data this package ships, the MORIE project keeps databases materialised from Google BigQuery public datasets (Chicago crime, EPA air quality, US census, FEC, FDA, NOAA, NHTSA, Hacker News, Ethereum, World Bank, ...) and serves their tables from the edge. They need no sign-in and no key; a key that an earlier version of this or a related package stored is not read and never sent. hostcat() returns every table with its key, description, rows and BigQuery source (the manifest is kept for a day); tables whose source terms do not allow redistribution (ICPSR studies, among them the NCVS 38604 extract, and any table the manifest marks restricted) are not served: they are left out, with a message counting them, and hostload() refuses them before any request. A table is served only when its access mark, if any, is "open" or "public" and its restricted mark, if any, is false; a mark of any other value or shape counts as restricted. hostload() checks each table against the SHA-256 the manifest lists for it (sha256_gz, sha256 or sha) and refuses a file that does not match; a table listed without any digest is used with a warning, once per session. hostload("db/table") returns one table, cached under the package cache directory (tempdir() unless options(rmoriedata.cache_dir = ) names a persistent one).

Usage

hostcat(refresh = FALSE)

hostload(key, refresh = FALSE)

Arguments

refresh

Fetch again even when a day-old copy is cached.

key

A db/table key from the catalog: segments of ASCII letters, digits, _, - and ., none starting with a dot, joined by single slashes. Any other key is refused before anything is requested, and a manifest entry whose key is not of this form is not served.

Value

hostcat(): a data frame with key, name, rows (NA where the manifest gives no whole count) and source; hostload(): the table as a data frame.

Details

hostload() returns the table as the file holds it, as the bundled tables are read: the column names as written (as the manifest lists them); an empty field is missing in a logical or number column and "" in a text column (the text "NA" is a value). A column is logical, integer or double only when every value in it is written the way R writes such a value: TRUE or FALSE; whole numbers without a leading zero or a plus sign; for double, numbers without a leading zero, whole ones of at most 15 digits (which a double holds exactly) and decimal ones of at most 17 significant digits (zeros after the decimal point are formatting, and "6.0" is 6), or in R's own exponent form (1e-05). Any other column is text, so a code such as "046" keeps its leading zero, and "+3", ".5", "0x1A", "Inf" or an identifier of 16 or more digits keep every character. A column with no value at all is logical NA. Text is marked UTF-8, whatever the session's locale; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are marked "bytes", and a NUL byte, which no R string holds, is dropped. Quoted fields may hold commas, quotes and line breaks (a Windows line end inside a field reads as "\n"); Windows line ends and a byte-order mark are allowed. A record with more or fewer fields than the header is a damaged download: the copy is deleted and the call fails, so the next call fetches it again.

The manifest is fetched again once the cached copy is a day old. When that fails (offline, or the service is down) the cached copy is used, with a message, so a table already cached in a persistent rmoriedata.cache_dir still loads offline; every table is still checked against the digest the manifest lists, and one that does not match is not used. With refresh = TRUE the manifest must be fetched: when it cannot be, hostcat() and hostload() stop with an error instead of using the cached copy.

R sessions loading the same table take turns: while one downloads it, or checks its cached copy, the others wait. A session whose wait sees the download not grow for options(rmoriedata.lockwait = ) seconds (600 by default) stops with an error saying the other session may be stalled.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
head(hostcat())
df <- hostload("chicago_crime/incidents")
} # }
